data.title: Country music star Zach Bryan buys $18 million, 40-acre Tennessee estate after getting married
data.description:
By Kelsi Karruli

Bryan reportedly bought the property earlier this year; it has a huge barn with a recording studio.

Zach Bryan performs September 2026.

Country star Zach Bryan has reportedly forked over $18.25 million for a sprawling estate in Franklin, Tenn.-months after tying the knot with Samantha Leonard.

Bryan, 30-who said "I do" in late 2025 following his highly publicized and tumultuous romance with influencer Brianna "Chickenfry" LaPaglia-picked up the palatial property earlier this year, according to TMZ.

Reportedly set on 40 acres, the estate offers plenty of privacy for the musician and his new wife, along with an impressive space for Bryan to work on his music in the comfort of his home.

Zach Bryan and Brianna LaPaglia in 2024 in Los Angeles.

The main residence spans 5,035 square feet and features four bedrooms and five bathrooms, along with a wraparound porch with unencumbered views of the surrounding Tennessee hills.

The expansive grounds are outfitted with two ponds, lush gardens, and walking trails, as well as a resort-style swimming pool and an outdoor kitchen.

However, one of the property's most impressive features is an enormous 5,300-square-foot barn.

Far from a traditional agricultural structure, the barn has been transformed into an entertainment and creative hub, complete with a grand bar, video wall, fireplaces, a game room, gym, and catering kitchen.

There are also two bedroom suites and a two-car garage.

Perhaps most fittingly for its Grammy-winning new owner, the barn boasts a massive recording studio, allowing Bryan to work on new music just steps from his home.

News of the singer's splashy purchase comes months after he and Leonard got married in Spain in late 2025.

The pair were first romantically linked in summer 2025. Their marriage marked a new chapter for Bryan after his messy and very public breakup with LaPaglia, who previously claimed that she had been offered millions of dollars-and, at one point, Bryan's Massachusetts home-in exchange for remaining silent about their relationship.

In July 2025, the former couple's breakup once again spilled into the public eye when Bryan shared screenshots of messages he claimed LaPaglia had sent after their romance ended.

One screenshot appeared to show a lengthy message from LaPaglia reflecting on her feelings about their 2024 split. In it, she said she would "never forget the love" she once felt for Bryan and insisted that she had never been interested in his "lifestyle or money."

She also wrote that she believed she "deserved a goodbye" and asked Bryan to take care of their shared cat, Stump, and give his dog, Jack, a hug on her behalf.

More from Realtor.com: Squatters Take Over $4.4 Million San Francisco Mansion With Bizarre Ownership History

Bryan also posted a screenshot of another message that appeared to have been sent by LaPaglia to a third party and outlined several alleged "options" available to her in the aftermath of the breakup.

One purported option involved taking a $12 million payment to stay publicly silent about the split. Another was accepting Bryan's Duxbury home in exchange for dropping allegations about their relationship. The final option was a "messy war," where LaPaglia would go public with her experiences.

Bryan quickly deleted the screenshots, but LaPaglia responded with several posts of her own, including what she claimed was a message from Bryan's manager detailing potential terms of an NDA.

According to the screenshot she shared, one proposed deal involved Bryan's "Duxbury house + 3 million," while another involved a $10 million cash payment.

More from Realtor.com: How I used a VA Assumable Loan to Buy a 3-Bedroom Home in San Antonio-and My Monthly Mortgage is $980

LaPaglia later insisted that she had "not told one lie ever" about her relationship with Bryan and claimed that she had ultimately turned down an offer worth $12.9 million.

At the time of their breakup, LaPaglia had been living in Bryan's $7.45 million Massachusetts mansion, which the singer purchased in April 2024.

By November of that year, a moving truck had been spotted outside the property, and LaPaglia later revealed that she had moved out and was searching for a place of her own in New York City-a process she documented on TikTok.

More from Realtor.com: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear Says Next President Must Make 'Bold Investment' in Housing

The Duxbury Bay mansion is believed to be the property referenced in one of the alleged post-breakup offers.

The waterfront residence boasts sweeping views of the bay, along with a private boathouse and pier.

Inside, it has five bedrooms and 6.5 bathrooms, as well as an expanded living space with a fireplace and a spacious kitchen.

Before Bryan purchased the property, it had spent nearly a year on the market and was listed for $8.9 million in August 2023.

More from Realtor.com: The Hidden Gem Short-Term Rental Markets of 2026: Where Owners Are Maximizing Returns

Bryan owns another property nearby, according to records, which show that a second Duxbury home was purchased for $1.4 million in August 2024 through the same LLC used for the waterfront estate. Bryan is listed as a manager of the LLC.

That residence sits closer to the center of town, roughly a four-minute drive from the Duxbury Bay mansion. Built in 1910, the property features three bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms.

This story originally ran on Realtor.com.

data.title: Packaging Expert Kyle Reger Explains Cost-Effective Packaging Beyond Box Prices in HelloNation
data.description:
Packaging Expert Kyle Reger Explains Cost-Effective Packaging Beyond Box Prices in HelloNation

Packaging Expert Kyle Reger Explains Cost-Effective Packaging Beyond Box Prices in HelloNation

PR Newswire

ROCHESTER, N.Y., Oct. 9, 2026

The Article Examines How Packaging Choices Affect Shipping Costs, Product Protection, Labor Efficiency, Storage, and Long-Term Operating Expenses.

ROCHESTER, N.Y., Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What makes packaging truly cost-effective? HelloNation answers that question inan article featuring insights from Packaging Expert Kyle Reger, Regional Sales Manager at Jamestown Container Companies in Rochester, New York.

The article explains that evaluating cost-effective packaging requires looking beyond the price of an individual box. While procurement teams often start with the purchase price, the article notes that packaging decisions affect nearly every step of the supply chain. Shipping efficiency, product protection, labor requirements, storage needs, and overall operational performance all contribute to the total cost of ownership.

According to the HelloNation article, one of the most significant factors influencing packaging costs is product protection. Packaging that fits products properly helps reduce damage during transportation and handling. Fewer damaged shipments can lower replacement expenses, reduce return shipping, minimize customer service issues, and prevent production delays. The article explains that even modest improvements in damage rates can create substantial savings when spread across large shipping volumes.

The article also describes how packaging design directly influences shipping costs. Oversized boxes often increase dimensional freight charges while requiring additional filler materials. Right-sized packaging improves freight efficiency by maximizing trailer space, increasing pallet utilization, and moving more products in fewer shipments. These improvements help organizations control transportation expenses while maintaining reliable product protection throughout delivery.

The HelloNation article emphasizes that packaging evaluations should carefully consider labor costs. Packaging that assembles quickly or simplifies packing lets employees work more efficiently. Small improvements in box design or packing methods can reduce repetitive tasks and speed up production. Over thousands of shipments, saving only a few seconds per package may translate into meaningful labor savings for many organizations.

Storage efficiency is another area where packaging choices influence long-term value. The article explains that packaging designed to nest efficiently or ship flat can reduce the amount of storage space required for inventory. Better organization also makes packaging materials easier to access during daily operations, helping warehouse teams work more efficiently while reducing unnecessary handling.

Throughout the article, Packaging Expert Kyle Reger explains that procurement decisions should consider the full operational impact of packaging, not just the initial purchase price. The article encourages procurement teams to compare product damage rates, freight expenses, labor efficiency, storage capacity, packaging consistency, and compatibility with existing workflows. Considering all these factors together provides a clearer picture of total packaging costs.

The article further notes that successful packaging decisions come from understanding how every stage of the supply chain connects to the next. Poorly fitting packaging may create unnecessary waste, require excess packing materials, slow production, increase freight expenses, or contribute to avoidable product damage. By considering the broader operational picture, organizations can identify cost-effective packaging solutions that improve efficiency while supporting dependable day-to-day operations.

What Makes Packaging Cost-Effective Beyond the Box Price features insights from Kyle Reger, a packaging expert in Rochester, New York, on HelloNation.

About Jamestown Container Companies

Jamestown Container Companies is a family-owned packaging manufacturer headquartered in Falconer, New York. Since 1956, the company has provided custom corrugated packaging, packaging supplies, displays, and contract packaging services to customers throughout the Great Lakes region. Jamestown Container Companies operates multiple facilities across New York and Ohio and is committed to delivering innovative, cost-effective, and environmentally responsible packaging solutions.

About HelloNation

HelloNation is America's Good News Network, a premier media platform built on the idea that good news travels faster when real people tell real stories. Through its community-focused publications and innovative "edvertising" approach, HelloNation delivers content that informs, inspires, and spotlights the leaders making a meaningful impact in their communities.

data.title: Oil Prices Steady After Trump Appears to Rule Out Iran Strikes Before Midterms — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid and Anthony Harrup 




  Oil prices recovered from early losses and settled slightly higher Friday as traders weighed President Trump's pledge not to attack Iran before the U.S. midterm elections against persistent shipping risks in the Persian Gulf and extensive offshore production shut-ins in the Gulf of Mexico. 



  December Brent crude futures edged up 0.4%, to $104.72 a barrel, for a 2.4% weekly gain. West Texas Intermediate crude for November delivery rose 0.4%, to $91.85 a barrel, up 0.8% on the week. 



  Trump said Thursday that the U.S. wouldn't attack Iran before the November midterm elections, citing what he called "productive discussions" with Tehran. The U.S. naval blockade of Iran remains in place, with roughly a dozen Navy ships in the region, The Wall Street Journal reported. 



  Oil prices are likely to remain elevated in the short term as risks to Middle East shipping routes persist and U.S. offshore production remains disrupted, said Hani Abuagla, a senior market analyst at XTB MENA. 



  Analysts at MUFG said geopolitical risks remain high amid fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, while shipping through the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz continues to face threats. 



  Brent's spread between the first two futures months remains in backwardation at around $3 a barrel, indicating continued tightness in the near-term market, they said. Backwardation is when near-term oil futures trade at a premium to contracts for later delivery, typically indicating tighter supplies in the immediate market. 



  Goldman Sachs estimated that Brent's geopolitical risk premium reached $22 a barrel in September, the second-highest monthly level on record and above the peak of $16 during the Russia-Ukraine war in 2022. The bank also estimated that a 100 million-barrel decline in commercial inventories across OECD countries raised Brent's fair value by nearly $8 a barrel. 



  Tensions elsewhere in the region also remain high. Iran and its Houthi allies in Yemen carried out another series of attacks Wednesday night and Thursday, including strikes targeting shipping in the Persian Gulf and Saudi Arabia, the Journal reported. 



  The U.S. also increased economic pressure on Tehran on Thursday. The Treasury Department sanctioned 17 vessels it said were part of Iran's remaining shadow fleet and had transported millions of barrels of Iranian crude, petroleum and petrochemical products to markets in South and East Asia. 



  Meanwhile, Hurricane Isaias increased disruptions to U.S. Gulf production. The storm reached Category 3 with winds of 120 mph as it approached the U.S. coast, and was expected to make landfall in Alabama "at or near major hurricane strength" Friday evening, according to the National Hurricane Center. 



  The Marine Minerals Administration said nearly 1.5 million barrels a day of oil and 1.3 billion cubic feet a day of natural gas had been shut in as of midday Friday, equivalent to 71.5% of current Gulf oil output and 58.8% of natural gas output. 



  The threat to U.S. Gulf Coast refineries has narrowed despite the offshore shutdowns. Less than 500,000 barrels a day of refining capacity in Alabama and Mississippi were at risk of a direct hit, down from 2.5 million barrels a day expected earlier in the week, S&P Global Energy said. Port closures and shipping delays could still disrupt refined-product exports, with U.S. Gulf Coast diesel exports averaging 1.4 million barrels a day so far this week, down from 2.1 million barrels a day the previous week, S&P said. 



  U.S. refineries appeared to have dodged a threat from the storm, Robert Yawger, a commodity specialist at Mizuho Securities USA, said in a note. 



  With production at record levels near 14 million barrels a day, "the U.S. can afford to take a few barrels of offshore production offline," he said. "But it can't afford to lose refining capacity with winter heating oil season on the horizon and distillate storage testing many-year lows."

data.title: Investor Alert: Robbins LLP Informs Investors of the Netcapital Inc. Class Action Lawsuit
data.description:
Investor Alert: Robbins LLP Informs Investors of the Netcapital Inc. Class Action Lawsuit

Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP informs investors that a class action was filed on behalf of persons or entities who purchased or otherwise acquired Netcapital Inc. (NASDAQ: NCPL) securities between December 15, 2021 and September 3, 2026, inclusive (the “Class Period”). Netcapital Inc. operates as a fintech company with a technology platform that allows private companies to raise capital online and provides private equity investment opportunities to investors in the United States.

The complaint alleges that Netcapital engaged in a fraudulent scheme to overstate its revenue through sham, backdated, and forged consulting agreements.

Investors who purchased Netcapital Inc. securities during the Class Period and suffered significant losses should contact Robbins LLP for information about the lawsuit and the December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff motion deadline.

Why Was Netcapital Sued?

The complaint alleges that, during the Class Period, defendants failed to disclose that:

(1) Netcapital improperly recognized material revenues from sham consulting agreements with entities controlled by defendant John Fanning;
(2) the consulting agreements were backdated and, in some cases, forged, and Netcapital Advisors provided little if any meaningful consulting services;
(3) the Portfolio Company transactions were improperly undisclosed related-party transactions involving John Fanning;
(4) Netcapital’s certifications pursuant to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 were false; and
(5) as a result, defendants’ statements about Netcapital’s business, operations, and prospects were materially false and misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

Why Did Netcapital Stock Drop?

Plaintiff alleges that on August 10, 2026, the SEC filed a complaint against Netcapital and certain individual defendants in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts, charging defendants with conducting a fraudulent scheme to overstate Netcapital’s revenue through sham, backdated, and in some cases forged consulting agreements between Netcapital Advisors and at least eleven Portfolio Companies controlled by Fanning. On this news, the price of Netcapital stock fell by just over $0.05, or 12.8%, to close at $0.3501 on August 11, 2026.

Then, on August 17, 2026, the Company filed a Current Report on Form 8-K with the SEC disclosing that the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm, Fruci & Associates II, PLLC, had resigned. On this news, the price of Netcapital stock fell by $0.0914, or 28.6%, to close at $0.2280 on August 18, 2026.

On September 3, 2026, after market close, Netcapital filed a Current Report on Form 8-K with the SEC disclosing that Avi Liss had resigned on August 27, 2026, effective immediately, from the Board of Directors and all Board committees on which he served, including the Audit Committee. On this news, Netcapital stock fell $0.0512 per share, or 8.14%, to close at $0.5774 per share on September 4, 2026. The following trading day, Netcapital stock fell a further $0.0759 per share, or 13.1%, to close at $0.5015 per share on September 8, 2026.

What Can Netcapital Shareholders Do Now?

Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Netcapital Inc. securities during the Class Period may be eligible to serve as lead plaintiff. The lead plaintiff is a court-appointed investor who represents the interests of all class members throughout the litigation. Stockholders who wish to seek appointment as lead plaintiff must move the court no later than December 7, 2026. Contact Robbins LLP for information about the appointment process.

Shareholders do not need to serve as lead plaintiff to share in any potential recovery. Investors who do not seek appointment may remain absent class members.

Does It Cost Anything to Participate?

No. Robbins LLP represents investors on a contingency fee basis, with no upfront or out-of-pocket fees or expenses.

Contact Robbins LLP

Investors seeking additional information about the Netcapital Inc. securities class action may contact Robbins LLP by submitting an inquiry, emailing attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr., or calling (800) 350-6003.

Why Robbins LLP?

A recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, Robbins LLP represents investors in securities fraud and shareholder derivative litigation. We have helped restore more than $2 billion in value to shareholders and secured some of the largest recoveries in shareholder derivative litigation history.

"Companies have an obligation to provide investors with complete and accurate information so that markets can function fairly and efficiently," said Brian J. Robbins, Founding Partner of Robbins LLP.

To be notified if a class action against Netcapital Inc. settles, or to receive free alerts when corporate executives engage in wrongdoing, sign up for Stock Watch today.

data.title: New to The Street Signs American Fusion (OTCQB: AMFN) to 12-Month National Media Series
data.description:
NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / October 9, 2026 / New to The Street, the long-running business TV and digital media platform for public and emerging companies, today announced it has signed American Fusion Inc. (OTCQB:AMFN) to a 12-month media series. American Fusion is the developer of the proprietary Texatron™ Fusion Engine™.

The program is built to raise American Fusion's profile with investors, institutions and the general public as the company moves its Texatron™ development and testing forward. It combines four channels into one coordinated campaign:

  • Earned media: earned media placements, plus professionally distributed global press releases each month.
  • TV commercials: national spots on Bloomberg Television and Fox Business Network, 30-second spots in the New York market (most of them during trading hours) and international Bloomberg commercials across the Middle East and North Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia.
  • NYC Times Square billboards: recurring placements on three 8-story billboards in Times Square, New York City.
  • Accredited-investor events: quarterly gatherings at Hudson Yards in New York City for retail brokers, analysts and accredited investors.

The series also includes monthly executive interviews filmed at New to The Street's NYC studios and regular national broadcasts on New to The Street's sponsored programming on Bloomberg Television and Fox Business Network. It adds a dedicated BIO show about American Fusion as sponsored programming on Bloomberg Television, plus distribution across the New to The Street YouTube ecosystem: more than 6.6 million subscribers across the New to The Street TV and NewsOut channels, the largest ecosystem for public companies.

"American Fusion is taking on one of the most important energy challenges of our time, and its story deserves a national stage," said Vince Caruso, Co-Founder and CEO of New to The Street. "This program puts the company in front of investors in every way they take in information: on television, in the press, on the streets of New York and face to face. We look forward to telling the American Fusion story over the next 12 months."

The first episodes and campaign elements are expected to roll out in the coming weeks.

About American Fusion Inc.
American Fusion Inc. (OTCQB: AMFN) is an advanced energy platform company focused on the development and commercialization of next-generation fusion energy technologies. The Company is advancing the Texatron™ Fusion Engine™ aneutronic fusion platform, designed for modular, infrastructure-grade deployment across industrial, commercial, defense and grid-constrained applications.
